name: Percolation
miniText: When can a locally transmitted disturbance continue through a disordered medium? NetLogo Percolation represents oil descending diagonally between hard soil cells, with probabilistic entry controlled by porosity. Its moving display tracks the active front and previously saturated cells. Broadbent and Hammersley establish the distinction between randomness in a medium and randomness of diffusing particles [1]. Domany and Kinzel connect cellular update rules with directed percolation [2], making directionality central rather than importing Fire's undirected connectivity threshold. Hinrichsen places extinction and sustained spreading within absorbing-state transitions [3]. This is a pedagogical stochastic lattice process: it omits pressure-driven flow, fluid conservation at physical scales, capillarity and measured soil structure. Repeated runs illustrate survival, stopping and finite-width variability; visual agreement with an oil plume is not empirical validation.

Registrant abstract consulted: ABSTRACT The paper studies, in a general way, how the random properties of a ‘medium’ influence the percolation of a ‘fluid’ through it. The treatment diifers from conventional diffusion theory, in which it is the random properties of the fluid that matter. Fluid and medium bear general interpretations: for example, solute diffusing through solvent, electrons migrating over an atomic lattice, molecules penetrating a porous solid, disease infecting a community, etc.
